extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, facility managers, HR and financial staff responsible for implementing parking policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and Q&A on implementing the draft OMB circular on parking facilities for federal agencies, covering objectives, applicability, thresholds, exceptions, and operational steps (carpooling, fee collection, allocation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of the circular
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular's objective is to conserve energy, improve air quality, and reduce unneeded subsidies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the stated policy goals that should guide decisions about parking valuation, fee collection, allocation, and any exceptions or local adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on employee union contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: It depends on the specific contract terms. Contracts should probably run their course. Upon renegotiation, the policy in this circular should apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing collective bargaining agreements are not automatically altered; agencies should honor current contract terms until renegotiation, at which point the circular's policy should be implemented as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSA determination of parking values
rubrics_metrics.description: Parking values will be determined this summer by GSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should rely on GSA valuation to determine whether parking facilities meet thresholds for charging; GSA valuations drive fee-policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with GSA carpool regulations for space allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency implements fee parking, will it still be required to comply with GSA carpool regulations for parking space allocation? A. Yes. The policy hopes to achieve even greater carpool use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee implementation does not remove obligations to follow GSA's carpool allocation rules; agencies should allocate spaces to support carpooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and accommodations for handicapped and nonstandard-schedule employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Handicapped employees and employees who frequently work hours different from an agency's normal-duty day will be allocated to such personnel without the requirement for carpool participation. Some modifications to the fee structure will be considered to handle individuals in compelling circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide allocations and make fee-structure adjustments for employees with disabilities or compelling scheduling needs; such individuals are not required to carpool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to contractor employees and gov-owned contractor-operated facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. The objectives of energy conservation and subsidy reduction still apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor employees using government-controlled parking and government-owned, contractor-operated facilities are within the policy's scope; agencies should apply the circular's objectives to those situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative branch coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative branch agencies: No. [Legislative branch agencies are not covered.] Requested to consider a similar policy for the legislative branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft circular does not apply to legislative branch agencies, but the legislative branch is encouraged to adopt similar policies voluntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: $10.00 monthly valuation threshold (and local flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency's parking spaces are valued by GSA at less than $10.00 a month and the agency believes that passing these costs through to the user would encourage ridesharing, may the agency charge that fee? A. Yes. The $10.00 threshold was selected because the policy applies nationwide. If local circumstances suggest that a lower threshold would be effective, it may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The $10/month valuation is the nationwide default; agencies may adopt a lower local threshold where justified to encourage ridesharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope estimate (number of spaces affected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary estimates are in the 120-130,000 range. Almost 20-25% of these are in the Washington, D.C., area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these estimates for planning and resource allocation; they are preliminary and informational rather than prescriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitor parking and public access
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may continue existing practice in setting aside certain areas so that the public may have reasonable access to the agency. The policy recognizes that one-time or occasional visitors would not have the opportunity to join a carpool for that visit, and that a one-time parking fee would not discourage the trip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should preserve reasonable visitor access; one-time visitors are effectively exempted from carpool requirements and agencies should consider existing practices when setting visitor parking policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee collection methods and implementing regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: How does an agency establish a means for collecting fees from users of its parking spaces? A. This subject will be addressed in the implementing regulations to be issued by GSA. Agency financial management staff should be able to provide advice on this subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should await GSA implementing regulations for detailed procedures; meanwhile consult agency financial management staff for interim guidance on fee collection mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources for carpool program setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Where can an agency obtain information on how to set up a carpool program? A. The Federal Highway Administration and the GSA Public Buildings Service will be able to provide material on this subject. The Tennessee Valley Authority also has an excellent program in operation in Knoxville, Tennessee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consult FHWA, GSA Public Buildings Service, and examples like TVA for practical materials and models for carpool programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives and operational steps when parking is abundant
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency location has an abundance of parking spaces, how will employees have an incentive to form carpools? A. Agency facility managers will allocate spaces near work site entrances to carpools and organize carpool matching programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preferential near-entrance parking and active carpool-matching programs as operational incentives to encourage carpools where spaces are plentiful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical reduction of parking spaces as enforcement/encouragement tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical reductions [in] parking space may be considered in some circumstances if a demonstrated increase in carpooling is not realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other measures fail to increase carpooling, agencies may consider removing parking supply as a policy lever to encourage ridesharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging when transit service is poor
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency does not have good transit service available, must a fee still be charged? A. Yes, if the facility cost exceeds the $10.00 monthly threshold. Agencies are encouraged to deal directly with the transit authority or company which provides transit services in their city to discuss improvements to transit routes serving the government facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee application is based on facility cost regardless of current transit quality; agencies should nonetheless pursue transit improvements with local providers when transit is poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of high-profile facilities (White House and Pentagon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this policy apply to the White House and the Pentagon? A. The draft circular applies to those facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-profile executive facilities are explicitly within the scope of the draft circular; apply the same rules unless otherwise specified in final guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explaining benefits to employees (messaging guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: How can I explain to my employees that this policy will be in their best interests? A. ... many employees already use transit or pay to park ... a good number of attractive parking spaces now used by single occupant cars will become available for carpools. This will benefit those employees who have not been able to qualify for government parking. Also, the individual in a carpool will only face one-third or one-fourth of the parking fee where a fee is in effect, and avoid the cost of driving his or her car at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these benefits—expanded access to attractive spaces, cost-sharing in carpools, and reduced driving costs—as key messages when communicating the policy to employees.
